title: Lodi Dynasty
capsule: The Lodi dynasty was the fifth and final ruling house of the Delhi Sultanate, founded when the Afghan chief Bahlul Lodi seized the throne in 1451, displacing the Sayyid dynasty. Sikandar Lodi (r. 1489–1517) consolidated the sultanate's authority across the Gangetic plain, founded Agra in 1504 as a second capital, and promoted Persian culture while enforcing harsh measures against Hindu practices. Ibrahim Lodi (r. 1517–1526) faced simultaneous revolts by Afghan nobles and an invitation to Babur by the governor of Punjab; Babur's Timurid army defeated and killed Ibrahim at the First Battle of Panipat on 21 April 1526, ending the Lodi sultanate and founding the Mughal Empire.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Lodi sultanate's core territories in the upper Gangetic plain are well documented in Persian chronicles and Mughal retrospective records; peripheral tributaries and exact northern and southern frontier lines are less precisely known.
